correctness.rationale: The four arcs for two triple events are distinct; contract them to a balanced graph, count cyclic Euler tours using BEST, compute the rooted Matrix-Tree cofactor by a two-column rank update, and calculate single-event marginals by one-column update. The four possible injective partial-match types are exhaustive. Exact symbolic covariance signs prove the q=5 nonnegative and q=6 strict boundaries. Independent tour enumeration at q=3,4 and fully separate integer cofactor computations at q=3–6 agree with all formulas. No finite testing is substituted for the proof.

originality.rationale: The final novelty claim is the all-alphabet sign taxonomy, sharp q=5 nonnegative cutoff, q=6 strict cutoff, and complete zero/negative classes. Rødland (2006) Theorems 1 and 3 already give general joint count identities and include our raw two-pattern probability as a specialization, and Cowan gives individual expectations; no originality is assigned to those formulas. Relevant primary full texts/sections, targeted web searches, research-record queries and 73 accessible previous claims revealed no statement of this four-case sharp sign law. A possible unindexed deduction from exact joint-count literature remains a substantive residual risk.
residual_risks: A general 2006 exact joint-count theorem implies the pointwise formulas. The all-q covariance-sign threshold may have been implicitly deduced, tabulated or stated in unindexed literature; this is the principal novelty risk.
Not all papers on conditional pattern correlations can be exhaustively surveyed within this review.
The theorem does not address overlapping edge prescriptions, different centers or higher de Bruijn order.
